title: The Fifth Cylinder
question: Today, can the narrator keep the curate alive while finding a route through the invasion?
light: violet lightning from the west, black shadows
palette: black ash, smoke grey, bruised green, copper, crimson fire, deep blue night

sunbury_dust.described: A straight country road enters Sunbury through hedges and scattered cottages. Black cindery dust covers the road, cart tracks, hedge leaves and roof tiles. Overturned carts and luggage occupy the roadside, with a dead horse in the shafts at the near left edge. The dusted village church tower stands at the far end beneath a pale sky. Grey daylight falls from the upper left across the road and catches suspended ash. The route picture carries the bleak aftermath of Halliford into the first stage of their escape. A distant house window holds a moving figure and a small lamp. Grey daylight comes from the LEFT, low from the west, under the drifting smoke.

richmond_bridge.described: Richmond Bridge crosses the Thames on five pale stone arches. A balustraded parapet runs from the near left edge toward the far right, and dark river water passes beneath it. Red masses float below the central arch. Richmond town spreads up the far hill with orange fire above the roofs, while woods beyond Ham and Petersham burn across the water. Amber firelight falls from the far hill and violet evening sky fills the upper frame. The bridge gives the journey a narrow exposed crossing between ash-covered roads. A distant river bank and the burning town complete the view. The light comes from the RIGHT: amber firelight from burning Richmond on the hill.

kew_road.described: A suburban back garden near Kew holds a weathered wooden tool shed with its door open, flower pots and a rake. A shrubbery and gravel passage run beside a large house standing in its own grounds. Its metal hood rises above the roofs while the garden gate frames the foreground. Dusk light falls from the western sky across the shed roof and gravel. Leaves and the shed door move in the wind. Dusk light comes from the LEFT, low from the west beyond the roofs.

kew_garden.described: A walled kitchen garden lies beside the road toward Kew. A wooden gate opens in the near red-brick wall, and gravel paths lead between box-edged beds and espaliered pear trees. A stone well-head stands toward the center. A lean-to glasshouse catches faint starlight at the right edge. Along the far wall, a clipped yew hedge overhangs a deep dry ditch filled with leaves. Grey-violet twilight gives way to blue night across the meadow beyond the wall. The gate, well-head and ditch form a route from flight into concealment, while the garden walls close the fugitives from the road. Stars appear above the wall as the fugitives settle among the leaves. Dusk light comes from the LEFT, low from the west over the wall.

mortlake_kitchen.described: A small Victorian back kitchen lies half buried beneath a collapsed white house. A tongue of dark garden mould crosses the north window and flows over a deal table. A pale-green dresser with copper and tin vessels stands along the west wall. A black-leaded range with brass fittings occupies the east wall beneath coloured wall panels. The south wall breaks open around a heavy beam and a triangular aperture above rubble. Red quarry tiles carry crockery shards, plaster and brick grit. Grey daylight falls from the south aperture across the rubble and range. The buried room holds the last visible structure of the house, with the scullery door at the west side.

mortlake_scullery.described: A dark Victorian scullery adjoins the buried kitchen. Stone flags cover the floor, and limewashed brick walls surround a shallow brown sink beneath an earth-filled window. A black cast-iron pump stands beside the sink. In the north-west corner, a brick-built copper with a wooden lid stands beside split firewood and a deal cupboard holding bottles, tins and biscuits. Two plank doors with iron latches occupy the south wall, while the kitchen door opens at the east. Grey light enters from the kitchen doorway and falls across the flags toward the pantry doors. The room gives the survivors a concealed passage toward food, coal and the buried house interior. The faint kitchen doorway remains the only visible light.

source: And then followed such a concussion as I have never heard before or since. So close on the heels of this as to seem instantaneous came a thud behind me, a clash of glass, a crash and rattle of falling masonry all about us, and the plaster of the ceiling came down upon us.
shots.turn: A room shelters them -> rubble seals them.
shots.why: The house becomes a prison, and the narrator (grey eyes, brown felt hat) loses the road he had chosen.

shots.end: The curate's face fills the upper LEFT frame edge; water touches the narrator's temple at the lower RIGHT frame edge; the vessel rests by the range; plaster glints across the tiles; the narrator's shoulders lift from the dust.
source: I was insensible for a long time, the curate told me, and when I came to we were in darkness again, and he, with a face wet, as I found afterwards, with blood from a cut forehead, was dabbing water over me.
shots.turn: Unconsciousness ends -> care restores awareness.
shots.why: The curate's care keeps the narrator (grey eyes, brown felt hat) alive, reversing the isolation of the opening.

source: Outside and very near was an intermittent, metallic rattle.
shots.turn: Quiet offers cover -> machinery announces proximity.
shots.why: The sound turns stillness into a warning, and the narrator (grey eyes, brown felt hat) must interpret what hearing cannot show.

source: “A Martian!” said the curate.
shots.turn: The sound puzzles them -> the creature gains a name.
shots.why: The curate supplies the immediate answer, while the narrator (grey eyes, brown felt hat) receives a threat he can finally name.

source: The window had been burst in by a mass of garden mould, which flowed over the table upon which we had been sitting and lay about our feet. Outside, the soil was banked high against the house.
shots.turn: Mystery becomes knowledge -> the ruins gain a cause.
shots.why: The ruined house becomes a cylinder's prison, and the narrator (grey eyes, brown felt hat) understands the scale of their entrapment.

shots.turn: Knowledge brings terror -> prayer fills the shelter.
shots.why: The world answers their discovery with machinery and vibration, while the curate gives voice to helplessness.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I resume my account inside a house cut off by black smoke.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Anxiety for my wife drove me through every room, then toward solitude.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The smoke reached the road and changed waiting into a calculation.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The curate repeated his safety, while I prepared for the open road.

lines.speaker: curate
lines.text: We are safe here.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I gathered food, drink, oil, rags, a hat, and a shirt.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Our road crossed ash, wreckage, fire, green grass, and bewildered survivors.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Under Richmond Bridge, red masses floated down the stream, some many feet across.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Three people ran toward the river, and up the hill Richmond burned.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Near Kew, a machine rose above the roofs and erased our route.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: We watched the machine seize its quarry, revealing purpose beyond destruction.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Night brought burned guns, thirst, and a house stocked for endurance.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I urged the curate to eat, choosing companionship over my former isolation.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: It can’t be midnight yet.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Glass clashed, masonry fell all about us, and the ceiling came down upon our heads.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The blow stunned me; the curate answered injury with water and care.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A metallic rattle made the buried room listen for an unseen visitor.

lines.speaker: curate
lines.text: A Martian!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: At dawn, the opening showed the house buried beneath soil, brick, and ruin.

lines.speaker: curate
lines.text: God have mercy upon us!
